Systems Programming and Machine Organization
Chapter 49: Producer–Consumer Systems: capacity, ownership, and closure
Dr. Charles Dorner

1. A queue transfers work and limits one stage
Problem and first experiment

SAY
A producer can generate work faster than a consumer can finish it. An unbounded queue turns that mismatch into growing memory use. A bounded queue limits the number of items waiting inside it, so a full queue must make the producer wait or reject the submission under an explicit contract. That is backpressure: the slower part influences the rate of incoming work. The queue is also an ownership boundary. Before a successful push, the producer owns the item; afterward, the queue does, until a consumer removes it. Start with those responsibilities before adding condition variables, because their predicates must express this state machine.

DO
Predict the concrete state or output before revealing the answer.
Explain which invariant and lifetime rule make the observation valid.

SOURCE
content/systems-programming/ch49.json → SP49.004

------------------------------------------------------------

2. Ring positions need a count to explain their meaning
Problem and first experiment

SAY
A ring buffer reuses a fixed array by wrapping indexes around its end. That saves moving every item after a removal. But an index pair alone can be ambiguous: the next insertion and removal positions may coincide when the buffer is empty or when all slots are occupied. Our demonstration stores a head and count, using their sum modulo capacity to find the insertion slot. The invariant keeps count between zero and capacity and head within the array. Logical order follows head, not physical index zero. Every field participating in that relationship needs one coordinated protection policy once producers and consumers run concurrently.

DO
Predict the concrete state or output before revealing the answer.
Explain which invariant and lifetime rule make the observation valid.

SOURCE
content/systems-programming/ch49.json → SP49.008

------------------------------------------------------------

3. Run a wraparound buffer without concurrency noise
Problem and first experiment

SAY
The ring first receives ten and twenty. Removing ten advances head to the next slot and reduces count. Inserting thirty and forty fills the ring and wraps one insertion to physical index zero. The remaining logical order is still twenty, thirty, forty, which the program prints after removed=10. This demonstration is a single-thread storage mechanism, not a synchronized producer-consumer queue. It isolates the representation invariant so a wrong wrap calculation is not confused with a waiting bug. A full push returns false before touching storage, and an empty pop returns no value. Later synchronization must protect head, count, and slots as one state.

DO
Predict the concrete state or output before revealing the answer.
Explain which invariant and lifetime rule make the observation valid.

4. A rejected submission must keep its owner
Problem and first experiment

SAY
This single-thread ownership model has one slot containing a unique_ptr. The first push transfers the seven-valued item into the slot and empties the caller's owner. The second push fails because the slot is full, leaving the nine-valued item with its caller. After closure, the accepted seven can still be moved out and drained, while another attempt to submit nine is rejected. The output records all those facts. A real concurrent queue would guard this decision and ownership transfer with the same mutex. Moving the item before checking capacity would make a failed push lose or destroy caller-owned work, so validation order is part of the resource contract.

DO
Predict the concrete state or output before revealing the answer.
Explain which invariant and lifetime rule make the observation valid.

The chapter problem

SAY

Begin with the complete chapter demonstration. It fixes the input so you can follow each change in state. After that trace is clear, the lab expands the contract: Implement a capacity-two queue with blocking push and pop. close rejects new pushes, wakes waiting participants, and permits consumers to drain existing items before reporting end.

6. Where the simple approach fails
The chapter problem

SAY
One wakeup rule is not enough: consumers need work; producers need space. Shutdown must also wake participants whose waits can no longer succeed.

A related failure in the generalized operation is concrete: In pop, return no value whenever closed_ is true, even if items_ is nonempty. Buffered work is lost during shutdown.

The repair changes the operation at the point where the rule can be enforced: After waiting, return no value only when the queue is empty. A closed queue can still contain items that the drain contract promises to deliver.

7. Mechanism, guarantees, and limits
The chapter problem

SAY
A class is useful here because the mutex, predicates, queue, capacity, and closed flag must obey one shared rule across several operations. All shared state is accessed under the mutex. Separate conditions describe available items and available space. The producer closes on normal completion and on exceptions so the consumer cannot wait forever for more input. The queue must outlive every participant.

A plausible alternative: An unbounded queue simplifies insertion but can turn overload into unbounded memory use.

8. Chapter 49 — Producer–Consumer Systems
Systems mechanisms and source lecture

SAY
A producer–consumer system separates creation of work from processing of work. A bounded queue connects the two rates and applies backpressure when producers get ahead. Its correctness requires more than a mutex around a container: it needs predicates, closure semantics, ownership rules, and a way for every waiter to terminate. The queue in this chapter stores integers in preallocated slots. That keeps allocation and throwing element moves out of push and pop , making the synchronization argument visible. A generic production queue must additionally define exception guarantees for its element type.

10. Producers
Systems mechanisms and source lecture

SAY
Producers create items and attempt to transfer them into the queue. A successful push transfers responsibility to the queue. A rejected push after closure leaves the caller responsible for whatever resource the item represents. Production rate should not be assumed lower than consumption rate. Bursts, slow downstream services, and failures can make the queue fill. Bounded capacity converts that condition into an explicit wait or rejection instead of unbounded memory growth.

DO

Use the source panel to inspect the complete original lesson and its exact wording.

SOURCE
content/systems-programming/ch49.json → SP49.004, SP49.005

------------------------------------------------------------

11. Consumers
Systems mechanisms and source lecture

SAY
Consumers wait for an available item, remove it under the queue’s protection, and process it outside the queue lock. Processing outside the lock lets other participants enqueue and dequeue while the current item is being handled. A consumer must distinguish temporarily empty from permanently closed-and-drained. Returning an empty result merely because no item is available at one instant would incorrectly terminate a worker while producers are still active.

12. Shared buffers
Systems mechanisms and source lecture

SAY
The shared buffer stores items not yet transferred to consumers. A ring buffer uses a fixed array with head and tail indexes. Count distinguishes empty from full when indexes alone are ambiguous. The invariant includes 0 <= count <= capacity , valid head and tail indexes, and a relationship between occupied slots and logical order. All fields that participate in that invariant use the same mutex in this implementation.

13. Bounded buffers
Systems mechanisms and source lecture

SAY
A bounded buffer has a fixed maximum number of queued items. It limits queue storage and provides a natural point for backpressure. It does not by itself limit all system resources: producers may hold items before pushing, and consumers may hold items while processing. Budget the complete pipeline. If each of 100 workers can retain a large item, a small queue does not imply a small total memory footprint. Capacity controls one ownership stage, not every live object in the process.

14. Buffer-full condition
Systems mechanisms and source lecture

SAY
A producer waits while the queue is full and still open. Its predicate is closed || count < capacity . Including closure ensures that shutdown can release producers that would otherwise wait forever for capacity. After waking, the producer checks closure before inserting. A notification does not reserve a slot for a particular producer; another producer may acquire the mutex first. The predicate loop handles that competition.

In plain English: This is a coordination rule that helps multiple workers share information without stepping on each other's work.

15. Buffer-empty condition
Systems mechanisms and source lecture

SAY
A consumer waits while the queue is empty and open. Its predicate is closed || count > 0 . If the queue is closed but still contains items, the consumer drains them under the policy used here. When closed and empty, pop returns no item, signaling normal completion. This is drain-on-close , not immediate cancellation. An aborting queue would need a different contract for queued and in-flight items.

In plain English: This is a coordination rule that helps multiple workers share information without stepping on each other's work.

16. Mutex synchronization
Systems mechanisms and source lecture

SAY
One mutex protects slots, indexes, count, and closure. The queue does not expose references to occupied slots after unlocking. Instead it copies an integer out while protected, then returns ownership of that value. The mutex also supplies visibility between the producer’s slot write and the consumer’s slot read. No extra atomic count is needed in this locked implementation. Adding atomics to already-protected fields can complicate the design without improving correctness.

In plain English: This is a coordination rule that helps multiple workers share information without stepping on each other's work.

17. Condition-variable synchronization
Systems mechanisms and source lecture

SAY
One condition variable represents the possibility of items becoming available; another represents capacity becoming available. Push notifies a consumer after insertion, and pop notifies a producer after removal. Closure notifies both groups. The predicates remain authoritative. Notifications happen after unlocking in this implementation, but state changes occur under the mutex. Queue destruction is permitted only after all producers and consumers have stopped using it; close is not an automatic join operation.

In plain English: This is a coordination rule that helps multiple workers share information without stepping on each other's work.

18. A bounded, drainable integer queue
Systems mechanisms and source lecture

SAY
Companion listing: ch49/bounded_queue.hpp Companion listing: ch49/main.cpp The expected sum is 5050. Capacity eight forces the implementation to support reuse of ring slots during the 100-item transfer. Scheduling determines exactly when participants wait; the correctness result does not depend on a particular waiting count. For arbitrary capacity values near size_t limits, even index increment needs range analysis. Here a successfully allocated vector<int> has a practical and implementation-constrained maximum well below a wrapping index increment. A more general storage abstraction should state and enforce its own maximum capacity explicitly.

19. Bounded buffer state transitions
Systems mechanisms and source lecture

SAY
For capacity 3, a producer must wait when the queue already contains three items. After a consumer removes one, size becomes two and a waiting producer may proceed. Conversely, a consumer waits when size is zero and can be notified after a producer inserts an item. One mutex protects the queue and its size predicate.

20. Why two predicates matter
Systems mechanisms and source lecture

SAY
A bounded queue has at least two logically distinct conditions: not-empty for consumers and not-full for producers. Using the same mutex is fine, but each side waits for the predicate that enables its operation. Notifications should be issued after state changes that can make the opposite predicate true.

Systems mechanisms and source lecture

SAY

Then extend the same queue to multiple producers and consumers. Force shutdown while a producer is blocked on a full queue and while a consumer is blocked on an empty queue. Give every attempted item a unique identity and track attempted, accepted, consumed, and rejected-after-close counts. Under the chapter’s drain-on-close contract, verify at quiescence that accepted = consumed and that each accepted identity appears exactly once. All workers must finish before queue destruction. Review 1. Why notify both producer and consumer waiters on close? Review 2. Does bounded queue capacity bound all in-flight memory?

24. The producer and consumer wait for different facts
Reason about the implementation

SAY
A producer may proceed when capacity is available, unless closure requires rejecting the request. Its wait predicate is closed or count less than capacity. A consumer may proceed when an item exists or closure tells it no future input will arrive. Its predicate is closed or count greater than zero. These are two different conditions over one protected state. The queue can use separate readable and writable condition variables while retaining one mutex for slots, indexes, count, and closure. Notification does not reserve space or an item, so each awakened participant rechecks its predicate before transferring ownership. Leaving closed out of either predicate can strand a waiter during shutdown.

DO
Predict the concrete state or output before revealing the answer.
Explain which invariant and lifetime rule make the observation valid.

SOURCE
content/systems-programming/ch49.json → SP49.012

------------------------------------------------------------

25. Drain-on-close is different from cancellation
Reason about the implementation

SAY
The chapter's queue uses drain-on-close. Closing prevents future pushes but does not discard accepted items. A consumer that sees closed with a nonempty queue still removes the next item. Only closed and empty means no more work will arrive and the consumer can finish. Immediate cancellation would need a different contract for queued items, in-flight work, and resource cleanup. Do not encode both meanings in one ambiguous Boolean without stating how each path behaves. Our ownership model drains seven after closure to make the distinction concrete. A caller who expects abort must not assume that close silently destroys every outstanding task.

DO
Predict the concrete state or output before revealing the answer.
Explain which invariant and lifetime rule make the observation valid.

SOURCE
content/systems-programming/ch49.json → SP49.014

------------------------------------------------------------

26. Capacity does not bound every live item
Reason about the implementation

SAY
A queue with capacity two can still participate in a system holding a hundred large items. Producers may allocate items before attempting push, and consumers may each retain one while processing. The queue bounds only the waiting stage it owns. To estimate memory use, include producer-held, queued, and consumer-held objects, plus any retries or caches. Backpressure should reach the stage that creates expensive resources if the overall budget matters. This is why ownership diagrams are useful alongside a ring-buffer diagram: one explains array occupancy, while the other explains all live items. A small count inside the queue is not a whole-process memory guarantee.

DO
Predict the concrete state or output before revealing the answer.
Explain which invariant and lifetime rule make the observation valid.

SOURCE
content/systems-programming/ch49.json → SP49.010

------------------------------------------------------------

27. Process outside the lock after taking ownership
Reason about the implementation

SAY
A consumer should hold the queue lock long enough to inspect state and transfer the next item's ownership, then process the item after unlocking. Otherwise a slow task prevents producers and other consumers from using the queue even when their operations are independent. Do not return a reference to an occupied slot and release the mutex while that slot can be reused. The consumer needs its own value or owning handle. This boundary also clarifies failures: once pop succeeds, the consumer owns the processing responsibility. A thrown processing exception is different from a queue-state failure and may require retry or reporting under the application's policy.

DO
Predict the concrete state or output before revealing the answer.
Explain which invariant and lifetime rule make the observation valid.

32. A bounded queue needs space, work, and shutdown rules
Code, diagrams, and debugging

SAY
A bounded queue needs space, work, and shutdown rules. A full queue rejects this push before changing its state. This baseline is a single-threaded model, not a blocking queue.

Model a queue with capacity two. Reject a third item, consume one, then permit another insertion.

The invariant is 0 <= size <= capacity. A real concurrent API must define whether full means wait, reject, or drop. Making space changes the condition that blocked producers care about.

A full queue rejects this push before changing its state. This baseline is a single-threaded model, not a blocking queue.

When space exists, append the value. Capacity must be checked and mutation performed under one lock in a concurrent version.

Return true only after accepting the value. The lab turns this contract into a bounded blocking queue with explicit closure and draining.

The queue size stays between zero and capacity. A rejected push does not discard existing data; the blocking lab adds explicit close and drain rules.

One wakeup rule is not enough: consumers need work; producers need space. Shutdown must also wake participants whose waits can no longer succeed. In the extended lab: In pop, return no value whenever closed_ is true, even if items_ is nonempty. Buffered work is lost during shutdown.

33. Wait, drain, then end
Code, diagrams, and debugging

SAY
This block is the blocking consumer operation.

Inside Queue::pop, after acquiring the queue mutex.

The persistent state decides whether to continue; a notification is only a reason to recheck that state.

wait temporarily releases the unique_lock while sleeping, then reacquires it. The lambda [&] borrows the queue state. It returns true if closure or an available item permits progress; the predicate is rechecked after wakeups.

The empty check occurs while holding the mutex. Only emptiness now returns nullopt. Closed but nonempty must continue so accepted items can drain.

Copy the oldest integer before removing it. Both operations happen within the same critical section.

Notify a blocked producer that capacity may be available. The producer must still reacquire the mutex and recheck its own predicate.

Return the removed value by value. The caller owns its copy after this function releases the lock.

Every items_ and closed_ access uses the queue mutex; accepted buffered items drain after close.

Returning immediately on closed_ loses buffered work. Waiting without the predicate can stall after an early notification.

DO
Explain each source line against the state it changes.

SOURCE
systems_labs/ch49/solution.cpp:33-37

42. Review the extension solution
Practice and extension

SAY
A class is useful here because the mutex, predicates, queue, capacity, and closed flag must obey one shared rule across several operations. All shared state is accessed under the mutex. Separate conditions describe available items and available space. The producer closes on normal completion and on exceptions so the consumer cannot wait forever for more input. The queue must outlive every participant. Repair principle: After waiting, return no value only when the queue is empty. A closed queue can still contain items that the drain contract promises to deliver.

Build the complete demonstration and compare every output character. The separate lab solution includes assertions for its named acceptance checks.

After waiting, return no value only when the queue is empty. A closed queue can still contain items that the drain contract promises to deliver.

DO
Compare your result with the exact expected output.
Review a boundary test and a failure path before accepting the design.

------------------------------------------------------------

44. Chapter summary and maintenance
Recall and transfer

SAY
A class is useful here because the mutex, predicates, queue, capacity, and closed flag must obey one shared rule across several operations. All shared state is accessed under the mutex. Separate conditions describe available items and available space. The producer closes on normal completion and on exceptions so the consumer cannot wait forever for more input. The queue must outlive every participant.

Choose a simpler approach when its narrower contract is enough. An unbounded queue simplifies insertion but can turn overload into unbounded memory use.

When this system changes, retain a check that exposes the known failure: In pop, return no value whenever closed_ is true, even if items_ is nonempty. Buffered work is lost during shutdown. After waiting, return no value only when the queue is empty. A closed queue can still contain items that the drain contract promises to deliver.

DO
Ask learners to identify the state, operation, and guarantee named on this page.
Use the source panel to inspect the complete original lesson and its exact wording.

SOURCE
content/systems-programming/ch49.json → SYS49.14

------------------------------------------------------------

45. Verify item identities as well as totals
Recall and transfer

SAY
A sum alone can miss a duplicate and an omission that cancel numerically. Give each attempted item a unique identity and track accepted, consumed, and rejected submissions. After all workers finish under drain-on-close, every accepted identity should appear exactly once among consumed items. Test capacity one, closing an empty queue, closing with queued items, and shutdown while producers or consumers are blocked. Closure must notify both waiter groups, and all users must stop before the queue's mutex and condition variables are destroyed. These tests connect the state machine to resource lifetime rather than merely checking that one demonstration prints the expected sum.

DO
Predict the concrete state or output before revealing the answer.
Explain which invariant and lifetime rule make the observation valid.

SOURCE
content/systems-programming/ch49.json → SP49.026

------------------------------------------------------------

46. Choose the queue contract before its implementation
Recall and transfer

SAY
A queue API should make clear what a successful push means. Usually it means the queue accepted responsibility, not that a consumer finished processing. State whether order is FIFO, whether full submission blocks, how closure releases waiters, and who keeps a rejected resource. Then choose a ring, deque, or other storage representation that fits the workload. A simple mutex-based queue provides a useful correctness baseline; a lock-free alternative still needs capacity, reclamation, and shutdown proofs. Maintain the same contract when replacing the implementation, and keep the original identity-based tests so a faster design cannot quietly change which work is accepted or discarded.

DO
Predict the concrete state or output before revealing the answer.
Explain which invariant and lifetime rule make the observation valid.

content/systems-programming/ch49.json → SP49.018
